Found it. On the two Meridian items (Insulated bottle A-100 and Field jacket B-200), you made $1,800 less gross profit in Q2 2026 (Apr-Jun) than Q1 2026 (Jan-Mar): $8,200 vs $10,000, about an 18% drop.

It's not a price thing, you're right, list price and actual sale price stayed flat at $30 (bottle) and $50 (jacket) all six months, and unit volume sold was identical both quarters (400 bottles, 200 jackets each quarter). Revenue was literally unchanged.

What moved was cost. Per Meridian Supply's terms, the volume tier a quarter's orders earn sets the unit cost for the next quarter, with the break at 500 units/quarter across all Meridian products. The Q1 2026 purchase order was cut from a planned 620 units down to 470 ("per cash plan", per the ledger memo), which landed under the 500-unit break. That dropped you into the higher-cost tier for Q2: A-100 cost went $15 → $18/unit, B-200 went $30 → $33/unit. Same volume, same prices, higher input cost, thinner margin.

So the fix, if you want Q3 margins back, is getting the next Meridian order back over 500 units/quarter, not touching price.

ANSWER: Gross profit on the Insulated bottle and Field jacket (both Meridian-supplied) fell $1,800 from Q1 2026 to Q2 2026 ($10,000 to $8,200), caused by a unit-cost increase from Meridian, not a price or volume change; the Q1 purchase order was cut to 470 units, missing Meridian's 500-unit/quarter volume break, which bumped Q2's per-unit cost from $15 to $18 (bottle) and $30 to $33 (jacket).
